diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: Diagnostics are different lenses, not one magic magnifying glass. Write the question you want answered, then choose a lens that can show that evidence.
diagnostics.html:
Diagnostics are different lenses, not one magic magnifying glass. Write the question you want answered, then choose a lens that can show that evidence.

  • Write down a specific question before picking a tool
  • Say what a profile shows and what a trace shows
  • Use len and cap as your first, cheapest evidence

profiling.title: Profiling
profiling.description: An allocation profile is a receipt book with different totals. Compare what remains in use with what has been allocated over the whole run.
profiling.html:
An allocation profile is a receipt book with different totals. Compare what remains in use with what has been allocated over the whole run.

  • Say the difference between in-use memory and total allocated memory
  • Explain why Mallocs keeps counting after old buffers are unused
  • Predict how the loop count changes the allocation total

tracing.title: Tracing
tracing.description: A trace is a timeline of footprints. Follow when work runs, waits and resumes instead of looking only at its final printed answer.
tracing.html:
A trace is a timeline of footprints. Follow when work runs, waits and resumes instead of looking only at its final printed answer.

  • Find the step where main blocks and the step where it resumes
  • Say what a trace shows that the final output cannot
  • Explain why one run does not show every possible order

runtime-stats-and-godebug.title: Runtime stats and GODEBUG
runtime-stats-and-godebug.description: Runtime statistics are labeled gauges on the same machine. Read the units and distinguish a live amount from a total that only increases.
runtime-stats-and-godebug.html:
Runtime statistics are labeled gauges on the same machine. Read the units and distinguish a live amount from a total that only increases.

  • Say what Alloc and TotalAlloc each count
  • Explain why they are equal here but drift apart later
  • Predict which of the two numbers can drop after a GC

benchmarks-and-allocations.title: Benchmarks and allocations
benchmarks-and-allocations.description: A benchmark is a repeated experiment with a clearly stated ruler. Count allocations for the same unit of work before comparing two implementations.
benchmarks-and-allocations.html:
A benchmark is a repeated experiment with a clearly stated ruler. Count allocations for the same unit of work before comparing two implementations.

  • Say what "allocations per operation" means for this loop
  • Explain why the count is 3 for three loop turns
  • Cut allocations by reusing one slice without changing the output

releases-what-changed-when.title: Releases: what changed when
releases-what-changed-when.description: A release note is a date on a rulebook. Read the date before deciding whether an older explanation still describes the behavior you are learning.
releases-what-changed-when.html:
A release note is a date on a rulebook. Read the date before deciding whether an older explanation still describes the behavior you are learning.

  • Say which Go version gave each loop turn its own i
  • Predict what closures saved inside a loop print today
  • Check a claim's Go version before trusting it
